gaps: P0: none. P2: none. P5: none.
notes: The 1778 watercolor is from the album ‘Voyage en Italie, en Sicile et à Malte’ (Niemeijer and De Booy 351); the album is mostly credited to Louis Ducros, but the record names no artist for this sheet, so it is given as unknown. It is drawn on three joined sheets with faint seams. B&H alternatives: #1 (1645 colored loose plate, higher resolution but torn through the Trapani strip), #3 (1582 German edition, book gutter through the view), #2 and #4 (uncolored; #4 is Palermo only). #7 (Parboni, 1845) shows the town only as a speck far off on the plain. #8 and #9 show the castle at Erice, not Trapani. #11 (1882) is a page of small vignettes. #13 (1891 wood engraving) copies the 1890 photograph. #14 (De Maria Bergler painting) is dated only ‘before 1900’. #16 and #18 are aerials of San Vito Lo Capo and Favignana; #15 is a wide 2023 seafront panorama, a possible P6 alternative.
